_comment: Roundtrip sequences driven against BOTH real abap2UI5 (upstream's node/ runtime:
official @abaplint transpiler over open-abap-core) and this port's engine, by
scripts/conformance.js. Each step is one POST; the draft id of a response is
threaded into the next step, so a scenario exercises the same state chain a
An app can only appear here if BOTH sides have it. That is why the list is
short: upstream's node/ build transpiles src/ only, so the shared surface is
the framework's own apps. The zcl_tst_* apps under upstream node/srv/ are the
obvious extension — they are purpose-built framework exercises (nav, popups,
sub-apps, binding) and they are app-layer ABAP, which is exactly what abap2js
transpiles well. See docs/adr-006-conformance.md, 'Growing the corpus'.
Keep steps minimal and deterministic. Anything that reads the clock, the
browser or a random source belongs in a scenario only if the normaliser in
conformance.js can already neutralise it — otherwise it produces a diff that
means nothing and trains people to ignore the gate.

steps.name: init
steps.comment: First roundtrip: no event, no draft. Exercises view building end to end — the builder chain, _bind (two-way) and _event wiring — and is the single densest comparison in the suite, because the whole view XML is one string that must match character for character.

steps.name: post-event
steps.comment: Applies a two-way delta and fires the event. Exercises main_json_to_attri (does the port write the edited value onto the deserialized app?) and message_box_display. The message text embeds the value, so a binding that silently did not arrive shows up as text, not as an absent field.

steps.name: init
steps.comment: The start page is what a user without ?app_start sees. It reads the draft table for its counters, so this step also compares what the two persistence layers report through the same view.

steps.name: init
steps.comment: Error path. A name that resolves nowhere must fail the SAME way on both sides — the framework's error view, not a stack trace and not a 500. Included because error behaviour is where a reimplementation drifts first and where nothing else in this repo compares the two.
